incident.location_detail: Lounge, door L-2, table 18
incident.evidence_of_threat: No anomalous readings, no creature sightings, no unexplained physical effects. The only measurements are ordinary: 22C ambient, maglock B at 41% battery with 24 of 40 flares, and motion counts consistent with a busy hack floor (31 events/min inside, 18 on the plaza side of the wall).
incident.ordinary_explanation: A mass voluntary relocation of attendees from the lounge to hack floor east because the submission form would not load on lounge Wi-Fi. The badge log (11 exits in 14 min, all toward hack floor east) and the radio call from table 18 corroborate a coordinated, self-directed move. The lounge headcount drop from 38 to 27, then down to 2 chair users and 4 staff, matches that flow. The 5 lounge windows with blinds half down and 18 motion events/min on the plaza side of the wall are consistent with people moving between the two areas. The maglock B battery at 41% with 24 of 40 flares is a maintenance issue, not a breach.
incident.summary: Lounge emptied as attendees moved to hack floor east to submit forms over better Wi-Fi; badge log and radio traffic confirm a voluntary relocation. No anomalous activity. Only open item is the courtyard maglock B battery at 41% (24 of 40 flares) with 34 minutes to the submission deadline.

incident.location_detail: Courtyard door at Entrance (525 Market), with figures on the landing (CAM 2) and plaza stair
incident.evidence_of_threat: Foam on the courtyard door is 5.5 hours old and flaking, with a hold estimate of 38% of rating; Maglock B is at 33% and dropping 2% per 5 min with actuator E41 repeating; entrance motion registers 96 events/min with 19 figures on the landing per CAM 2 and 3 more on the plaza stair; only 24 of 40 flares remain at 14 min burn each; 4 registration staff are holding the service door; radio reports only 2 foam canisters, enough for one door; door temp is 14C against a 22C hall; a PD unit has reported staging at Market and 1st.
incident.ordinary_explanation: Foam degradation and a failing maglock/actuator are consistent with ordinary equipment wear, and the 19 figures on the landing plus 3 on the plaza stair are consistent with the 237 attendees on the Loft floor moving through the entrance; the 14C door temperature against a 22C hall is consistent with an exterior door in cool air.
incident.summary: At the Entrance (525 Market) the courtyard door's foam seal is 5.5 hours old and flaking with a hold estimate of 38% of rating, Maglock B is down to 33% and falling 2% per 5 min, and actuator E41 is repeating. Motion shows 96 events/min with 19 figures on the landing per CAM 2 and 3 more on the plaza stair, while 4 registration staff hold the service door and radio reports only 2 foam canisters, enough for one door. Flares are down to 24 of 40 at 14 min burn each, door temp is 14C against a 22C hall, 237 people are on the Loft floor with 0 injured, dinner starts in 28 min, and a PD unit has just reported staging at Market and 1st. No creature is identified in the report; the readings are consistent with ordinary equipment wear and normal crowd movement, so the verdict is unclear pending confirmation of what the figures on the landing are doing.

incident.location_detail: Courtyard door and entrance (525 Market) — fire alarm horn and strobes, maglock B at 12%, door deflecting 6 cm, 61 figures converging on the courtyard door

civilians.location: Loft floor moving to stair A

incident.evidence_of_threat: Fire alarm re-triggered at 18:22 with horn at 102 dB and strobes active; entrance motion registering 388 events/min with 61 figures converging on the courtyard door; door deflecting 6 cm and maglock B down to 12%; 237 people on the Loft floor evacuating to stair A at ~40 per minute with landing density 4.8 per m2; lobby below holding 60+ figures with elevator doors open (Phase I); stair B door locked from the stair side with 0 people; two chair users and one oxygen user at the stair A landing.
incident.ordinary_explanation: A fire alarm activation during submissions closing would produce mass evacuation toward stair A, crowding at the lobby and elevator, and a radio call to cut the horn. The 61 figures converging on the courtyard door and the 6 cm door deflection with maglock B at 12% could reflect crowd pressure against a door whose lock is failing under load. Stair B being locked from the stair side is consistent with a fire-alarm egress protocol holding that route closed.
incident.summary: During submissions close, the tower fire alarm re-triggered at 18:22, sending 237 people on the Loft floor to stair A and jamming the lobby and elevator below. At the entrance, 61 figures converged on the courtyard door, which deflected 6 cm with maglock B at 12%. Stair B was locked from the stair side with no occupants, and two chair users plus one oxygen user were at the stair A landing. No creature is described; the readings are consistent with an alarm-driven evacuation and crowd pressure on a failing door, but the report does not confirm the alarm cause or the door's condition, so the verdict remains unclear.

incident.ordinary_explanation: unknown
incident.summary: At 18:29 the horn circuit was cut and at 18:30 the stair B doors on floors 3-5 were unlocked, after which wardens pushed the crowd up stair B; 168 people ended up on floor 5 in vacant suite 500 plus 7 from stair B, while 61 figures remain held at the courtyard door by 9 stacked tables after maglock B failed at 18:41. 69 people are still on the loft floor (lounge 27, main stage 24, hack floor east 8, closet 6, restroom corridor 2, 2 wardens at the service door), one evac chair is available for the 3 who cannot take stairs, and floor 5 is at 19C with one restroom and one case of water. No creature is described in the report; the threat is the deliberate disabling of alarms and locks and the resulting crush risk.
